subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should managed daemon installs use a fixed generated heap cap now, require a user-configurable heap surface first, or defer to diagnostics/manual wrapper guidance?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but choosing an 8192 MB default versus a CLI/config surface affects low-memory hosts, upgrade behavior, and the intentional NODE_OPTIONS security boundary.

options.title: Land fixed daemon heap headroom
options.body: Use the active PR's fixed generated heap value as the emergency availability mitigation and track tuning separately.

options.title: Require tunable heap surface first
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose and prove a CLI/config setting that survives reinstall and upgrades.

options.title: Diagnostics-only for now
options.body: Warn from status or doctor and rely on wrappers/manual service edits until live reproduction or resource policy is clearer.

recommendation.title: Land fixed daemon heap headroom
recommendation.body: Use the active PR's fixed generated heap value as the emergency availability mitigation and track tuning separately.
